source: Rasuwa-Bhotekoshi Flood: Search, Rescue and Relief Response, Situation Report #01
publisher: National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA), Government of Nepal
note: Figures from a live response move daily. Everything here is quoted as NDRRMA published it at the stated hour and is not adjusted, averaged or updated from reporting. Later situation reports supersede these numbers.

cause.statement: A major ice-rock avalanche in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China-Nepal border, about 20 km upstream of Rasuwagadhi.
cause.detached_material: an estimated 1 km2 section of rock-glacier material from a north-facing slope near the Lhende River
cause.became: entrained proglacial sediment and transformed into a highly mobile sediment- and water-laden debris flow
cause.seismic: A signal equivalent to greater than 5 Mw was recorded near Langtang/Lirung. NDRRMA state that subsequent analysis confirmed the signal was generated by the mass movement itself and was not the triggering cause.
cause.resolves: This is the primary account. Copernicus recorded the activation as a glacial lake outburst flood and the USGS first issued it as an earthquake before re-typing it a landslide.

timeline_local.what: The ice-rock avalanche reaches the Lhende Khola
The Bhote Koshi-Syafrubesi hydrological station stops transmitting, last water level 1.62 m
DHM confirms a major flood wave and issues downstream warnings along the Trishuli corridor
Peak discharge at Devghat, about 5,850 cubic metres per second

people.deaths_note: Deceased bodies and body parts recovered along the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli basin.
people.isolated_where: Gosaikunda and Amachhodingmo Rural Municipalities, Rasuwa
people.isolated_duration: up to six days without road connectivity, electricity or communication

damage.buildings_in_flood_zone_note: NDRRMA state this figure is estimated exposure from satellite mapping, not verified damage.
